intro: An AI assistant for procurement specialists is a voice helper that works in the apps you already use. Lazur is built for that job on the Mac. It sees your screen only while you hold the shortcut, points at the right control in Excel or Outlook, and drafts supplier emails. Below is where it helps and where you still do the work.
tldr: Procurement specialists spend most of the week on comparison, email and records. Lazur helps with each one, one question at a time.
Lazur points, guides, explains, dictates and drafts. It does not click buttons, edit files or send anything for you.
Public time data for this job is thin. The closest benchmark covers a different group of workers, so track your own week for a few days.
Check your company's rules before you share supplier pricing or contract terms with any AI tool.

blocks.text: A procurement specialist spends the day between suppliers, spreadsheets and inboxes. The core work is comparison, negotiation and record-keeping. Much of the time goes to the steps around that work. An assistant earns its place by answering one question about the screen you are on, then getting out of the way. That is the test used here.
What procurement specialists do all week

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics groups procurement specialists with buyers and purchasing agents. Its handbook lists the core duties. You compare suppliers on price, quality and delivery speed. You review price proposals and financial reports. You negotiate contracts and watch them for vendor compliance. You also keep records of purchases, costs, deliveries, product performance and inventory. Most of this happens in an office, with some travel to visit suppliers or review products.

items: Supplier comparison lives in quotes, PDFs, spreadsheets and email threads.
Price review lives in cost sheets and last quarter's files.
Contract monitoring lives in dates, clauses and vendor emails.
Records live in purchase systems, shared drives and your memory.

blocks.text: Where the time goes, and what the data says

Public time studies for procurement are thin. We could not find one that measures how much of the week goes to email, admin or typing for this job. The closest figure comes from a Parseur survey run in July 2025 among 500 U.S. professionals across many jobs. It found that people spend more than nine hours a week moving data from emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and scanned documents into systems.

That group was not procurement. Parseur's release does not mention procurement at all. Its heavy users, those who spend 20 or more hours a week on this data work, are more likely to sit in IT and finance. Treat the figure as a warning sign, not a measure of your week.

The fastest way to get your own number is a short log. Write down each block of the day for a few days. Group the entries into comparison, email, data entry, calls and research. Look for the group that repeats. Repeats are where an assistant saves you the most time.
A realistic procurement day with Lazur

The timeline on this page is a typical day, not a study. Each line is something you might say out loud to Lazur. The result shows what it does in reply. Notice how small most of these requests are. A chase email, a reminder and a menu question add up. None of them feels big enough to write down, which is why they eat the afternoon.
Compare supplier quotes in Excel without rebuilding the sheet

Say you hold quotes from two packaging suppliers. One lists a unit price and a minimum order. The other quotes per case, with freight added at checkout. Put both on the same basis before you compare anything. Convert each quote to cost per unit, delivered to your dock. A sheet with one row per cost item makes the gaps easy to see.

blocks.text: Formulas are the other common stumbling block. Ask Lazur to explain a lookup you did not write, such as an INDEX and MATCH pair on a supplier code. It explains the formula out loud and points at each argument. It does not rewrite the sheet. Type the change yourself, then test it on one row before you copy it down the column.
Draft supplier follow-ups in Outlook for Mac

Outlook for Mac is where supplier threads pile up. Microsoft's update history lists Outlook for Mac 16.114.4, build 26110224, released November 4, 2026. Yours may be older. Check it under Outlook > About Outlook before you follow any steps in this guide, because menus move between builds.

Drafting is where Lazur helps most for this job. Hold ⌥⌘ and describe the email. Name the order, the item and the date you need it by. Lazur drafts the text. You read it, fix the names and dates, and send it. The email goes out under your name, so the final check stays with you.

For longer notes, hold fn and speak. Dictation types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Before you use it on supplier work, open the personal dictionary and add supplier names and product codes. Otherwise a name like Northwind may come out as two words. Snippets help too. Save your standard payment terms as a snippet and call them up when you need them.
Shared inboxes, rules and follow-up tracking

Many procurement teams share one purchasing mailbox. A shared mailbox makes it easy for a supplier reply to sit unread. Add the shared mailbox first, then set up a rule that moves supplier replies to a folder. The steps are in our guides: [how to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook) and [how to create a rule in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook).
Research supplier and market prices without losing track of sources

Ask Lazur to research a material's recent price trend, or a supplier's certifications. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It returns a summary and a report. Treat both as a first draft. Open each source, check its date and confirm any figure before it reaches a negotiation.

items: Ask for the publisher and date behind every figure.
Ask which claims it could not confirm, and leave those out.
Ask for the exact page where a number appears, then open that page.
Save the report with its sources, not the summary alone.

blocks.text: Keep supplier data inside your company's rules

Supplier pricing, bid results and contract terms are often confidential. Your employer decides what can leave the company, and which tools may see it. Check with IT or legal before you share a quote or a signed contract with any AI tool, Lazur included. Ask what your team already allows, and write the answer down.

Here is what Lazur does with what it sees. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are product facts. They are not a compliance certification, and they do not replace your company's policy.
Set up Lazur on your Mac for procurement work

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. [Download Lazur](/download) and open it. Then hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question about the screen in front of you. Start with something low risk, like asking where a menu item sits in a blank sheet.

items: Check macOS first. Microsoft says Office versions 16.78 and later need macOS Monterey or newer.
Check Excel under Excel > About Excel, and Outlook under Outlook > About Outlook.
Build the personal dictionary before your first dictation at work.
Test everything on a practice file, not a live contract.
Ask IT whether AI tools may see supplier files on your screen.

blocks.text: Mistakes procurement teams make with an AI assistant

items: Pasting a confidential bid into a tool before checking the rules.
Trusting a total without checking one supplier by hand.
Expecting Lazur to click. It points and guides, and you do the clicks.
Dictating supplier names without a dictionary, then sending the email as typed.
Asking for research and never opening the sources.

blocks.text: The first mistake causes the most damage. Teams often add a tool before they agree what it can see. Write a short rule with IT. Name the files that stay out, such as bid evaluations and signed contracts. Then tell the team, and check the rule again when a new tool arrives.
Where Lazur fits beside your purchasing system

Lazur works beside your purchasing or ERP system, not inside it. Open the system, hold ⌥⌘, and ask where the approval button sits, or what a status code means. Lazur reads the screen you show it. It does not log in, submit an order or approve anything for you. Lazur has no partnership with any app maker, and it is not a plugin for any app.
Where to start this week

Pick one repeat task. Chasing late confirmations is a good start. Rebuilding the same quote comparison each month is another. Use Lazur on that task for a week, then decide whether it saved time. For the next step, read the [Excel guide for procurement specialists on Mac](/for/procurement-specialists/excel) and the [Outlook guide for procurement specialists on Mac](/for/procurement-specialists/outlook).

faq.question: What does an AI assistant for procurement specialists do on a Mac?
faq.answer: It sees the screen you show it while you hold the shortcut. It answers out loud, points at controls in Excel or Outlook, guides you one click at a time, and drafts or dictates text. It does not place orders or approve invoices.

faq.question: Can Lazur do the work in Excel and Outlook for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It circles where a control is, explains a formula, and drafts text. You make every change and send every email yourself.

faq.question: Is supplier pricing safe to share with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Whether you may share supplier pricing is your employer's decision, so check with IT or legal first.

faq.question: Which versions of Excel and Outlook does this work with?
faq.answer: Microsoft's update history lists Outlook for Mac and Excel for Mac 16.114.4, build 26110224, released November 4, 2026. Office versions 16.78 and later need macOS Monterey or newer. Check your own version under Excel > About Excel first.

faq.question: Does it work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Does Lazur connect to our ERP or purchasing system?
faq.answer: No. Lazur has no partnership with any app maker and is not a plugin for any app. It works with what is on your screen, so it can explain a field or point at a button in your system.

faq.question: How should a team start without disrupting work?
faq.answer: Pick one repeat task and use Lazur on it for a week. Keep a note of what it saved and what it got wrong. Then decide whether to widen the use.

painPoints.title: Quotes arrive in too many shapes
painPoints.text: Supplier quotes come as PDFs, attachments and pasted tables. Someone copies them into one sheet before any comparison starts. Parseur's survey found more than nine hours a week spent moving data by hand, though that group was not procurement.

painPoints.title: Price reviews start from a blank sheet
painPoints.text: Each review rebuilds last quarter's file. Formulas break when a supplier moves a column. Old figures stay in the file, and nobody notices until the total is wrong.

painPoints.title: Follow-up emails eat the afternoon
painPoints.text: Chasing a late confirmation or a missing invoice means the same email, with new dates, again and again. Each one takes a few minutes, and they add up fast.

painPoints.title: Records sit in too many places
painPoints.text: Purchase history, contract dates and delivery notes live in different tools. The gaps show up in an audit or in the middle of a negotiation.

painPoints.title: Admin crowds out the supplier call
painPoints.text: The negotiation gets whatever time is left. Dictation and drafting give some of it back, if you use them on the small tasks first.
